definition: Enmity means ill will, hatred, hostility.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word enmity. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know enmity should be able to work it out from your sentence.

Hatred is the broad word for the feeling itself, and it can attach to anything — a food, an idea, a stranger — with no relationship behind it. Enmity is hatred settled between particular parties: two sides who know each other, return the feeling, and have carried it long enough for it to become the relationship.

The two villages face each other across a narrow alpine valley, close enough to share weather and church bells.
Their enmity is nearly four hundred years old, older than any grievance anyone can document.
It is scrupulously mutual: each village schedules its festival on the other's, and neither cheese may be sold at the other's market.
